question.problem: An old computer has $4$ levers, each of which has $3$ positions. How many possible combinations of settings are there?
question.worked_solution:
The computer has $4$ levers, each of which has $3$ positions. Using the **rule of product**, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Total Number of Settings} & =\text{Number of positions of the }1\text{st lever} \\  & \times \text{Number of positions of the }2\text{nd lever} \\  & \times \text{Number of positions of the }3\text{rd lever} \\  & \times \text{Number of positions of the }4\text{th lever} \\  & =3\times 3\times 3\times 3 \\  & =81.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there are $81$ possible combinations of settings.
